You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — MPG Office Trust realized record after the March 2012 restructuring (fixed ~2015–2017 outcome window)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The registrant ceased to exist as a public company
> roughly eighteen months after the transaction, so no separate public periodic report
> exists within the fixed 3–5-year outcome window; that limitation is documented below.
> This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Fixed outcome window and public-reporting status
- The fixed outcome window for this case is the 3–5-year horizon after the ~2012 closing,
  i.e. approximately 2015–2017. [window fixed at construction]
- The registrant's last annual report on Form 10-K, for the fiscal year ended December 31,
  2012, was filed on 2013-03-18. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000017, Form 10-K (FY 2012)]
- The registrant filed a Form 15-12B on 2013-10-28, ending its Exchange Act reporting
  obligations; no Form 10-K, 20-F, or other periodic report was filed by the registrant
  within the fixed 2015–2017 window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000213, Form 15-12B]

## Terminal realized event within the observable public record
- On October 15, 2013, MPG Office Trust, Inc. was acquired: pursuant to an Agreement and
  Plan of Merger dated April 24, 2013, the Company merged with and into REIT Merger Sub
  (a subsidiary of Brookfield DTLA Holdings LLC, an indirect subsidiary of Brookfield
  Office Properties Inc.), with the surviving corporation renamed Brookfield DTLA Fund
  Office Trust Inc.; the Company ceased to exist. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Items 2.01 and 5.03]
- Each share of Company common stock outstanding at the effective time was canceled and
  converted into the right to receive $3.15 per share; aggregate consideration for common
  stock was approximately $181,251,680.40, and Sub REIT/REIT Merger Sub were capitalized
  through a $190 million cash contribution from Brookfield DTLA. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Items 2.01 and 5.01]
- The Company's 7.625% Series A Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock was subject to a
  cash tender offer at $25.00 per share (372,901 shares validly tendered and accepted);
  untendered shares were converted into Sub REIT preferred stock. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Item 2.01]
- The Company notified the NYSE that its common and preferred stock would be delisted, and
  requested Form 25 notifications of removal from listing effective after the close of
  trading on October 15, 2013. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Item 3.01]

## Management/organization at the terminal event
- Upon closing, all directors of the Company other than Robert M. Deutschman and Edward J.
  Ratinoff resigned, and officers of the acquiring merger sub became the officers of the
  surviving corporation — including Mitchell E. Rudin (President and CEO, US Commercial
  Operations), Bryan K. Davis (CFO), G. Mark Brown (Global Chief Investment Officer), and
  Paul L. Schulman (COO, US Commercial Operations). [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Item 5.02]
- The registrant's prior President and CEO (who signed the March 2012 closing filing) is
  not named among the surviving corporation's appointed officers, indicating the acquired
  entity's senior management did not continue running the surviving company. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Item 5.02] [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-12-000018, Form 8-K signature block]

## Realized 3–5-year trajectory of the specific transaction — not separately observable
- Because the registrant was acquired whole and deregistered roughly eighteen months after
  the March 2012 closing, there is no separate public periodic report disclosing the
  realized 3–5-year (2015–2017) trajectory of the retained joint-venture properties, and
  no segment disclosure of that business is available in a public filing of the registrant.
  On these facts the realized outcome over the fixed window is coded **uncertain**; it is
  neither fabricated nor inferred from any acquirer's consolidated results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000213, Form 15-12B] [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Item 2.01]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The single best-documented realized event is a whole-company acquisition: on October 15,
  2013 the registrant was merged into a Brookfield subsidiary, common shareholders received
  $3.15 per share (approximately $181.25 million in aggregate), the stock was delisted from
  the NYSE, the prior board and management were replaced, and the registrant deregistered
  via Form 15-12B on 2013-10-28 — after which no public periodic record exists for the
  fixed 2015–2017 window, so the transaction-specific 3–5-year outcome is coded uncertain. [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000197, Form 8-K Items 2.01, 3.01 and 5.02] [SRC: SEC accession 0001204560-13-000213, Form 15-12B]

[SLICE END]
